key_insight: Deep learning can infer optic nerve integrity traits from standard fundus photos, enabling much larger genetic studies that uncover new neurodegenerative loci.
clinical_relevance: This approach could expand glaucoma-related biomarker discovery using routinely collected eye images, especially where OCT is unavailable.
method: Trained AI to estimate pRNFL thickness and BMO-MRW from 2D fundus images.
Validated AI-derived traits against OCT measurements and then imputed them in UK Biobank and the Canadian Longitudinal Study on Aging.
Ran genetic association analyses to identify loci linked to the predicted phenotypes.
evidence_signal: AI-derived pRNFL and BMO-MRW correlated well with OCT measures (r=0.69 and 0.79), and the predicted traits showed strong genetic correlations with prior direct measurements (0.70 and 0.96).
watch_item: Because the phenotypes are inferred from images rather than directly measured, performance and transferability may vary across cameras, populations, and datasets.
paper_title: Genetic discovery using deep learning-derived optic nerve integrity phenotypes
